# University of Melbourne – Concise Summary
The University of Melbourne, established in 1853 in Victoria, Australia, is one of the country’s leading universities, consistently ranked first nationally and within the top 40 globally across multiple major rankings. Its primary Parkville campus is situated near Melbourne's CBD and forms part of a major knowledge precinct, with additional campuses dedicated to specialized disciplines including horticulture (Burnley), performing arts (Southbank), veterinary science (Werribee), forestry (Creswick), and agriculture (Dookie); a new engineering-focused campus at Fishermans Bend is slated to open in 2026. The university comprises nine faculties spanning architecture, arts, business, education, engineering/IT, fine arts/music, law, medicine/dentistry/health sciences, and science, and operates under governance from a university council with a vice-chancellor as chief executive.
Known for innovation in curriculum, the University of Melbourne implemented the “Melbourne Model” in 2008, organizing studies into broad undergraduate degrees followed by specialized graduate entry, a move that sparked sector-wide debate. The university has a large and diverse student body—including 44% international students—and offers nearly 40 undergraduate and graduate programs, supported by robust financial resources and an endowment exceeding $1.3 billion. Melbourne is recognized for its research excellence, innovative entrepreneurship initiatives, and extensive collections in libraries (holding over 3.5 million items) and museums. Student experience is shaped by over 200 clubs, a vibrant residential college network, and competitive sports teams. Notable alumni include Nobel laureates, multiple Australian prime ministers, and distinguished contributors to arts, science, and public life; in 2024, Emma Johnston was appointed as the first female vice-chancellor in its history.
